core: The product is the Raspberry Pi 3 Model B, a single-board computer with ARMv8 64-bit architecture and 1GB RAM.

It has built-in WiFi via a BCM43438 chip and Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) capabilities.
adjacent: The processor speed increased from 900 MHz on the Pi 2 to 1.2 GHz on the Pi 3.

99% of cases and accessories for Pi 3, Pi 2, and Pi B+ are compatible, though metal-topped cases may cause WiFi chip issues.
The product is available in both UK and China manufacturing locations with no advance notice of which will be shipped.
Although the chip is 64-bit ARMv8, Raspbian is only available in 32-bit ARMv7 compatible mode, and the OS may report as 32-bit ARMv7.
The only physical difference from Pi 2 is a slight change in LED placement.
The product SKU is 3055.
The item condition is listed as new.
BLE support was still in development at the time of this product page.
A 5V 2.4A power supply is noted as compatible and sufficient for the board with Ethernet and USB add-ons.

declared_fields.Recipe.description: Kids will love to help assemble this easiest ever pasta bake with streaky bacon, beef mince, a crème fraîche sauce and gooey mozzarella
declared_fields.Recipe.name: Easy classic lasagne
declared_fields.Recipe.author[0].name: Angela Boggiano
declared_fields.Recipe.headline: Easy classic lasagne
declared_fields.Recipe.keywords: 2 of 5-a-day, Angela Boggiano, Beef lasagne, Calcium, Children, Cooking with children, Cooking with kids, Family friendly, Kids, Lasagne, Spring
declared_fields.Recipe.publisher.name: Good Food
declared_fields.Recipe.recipeCategory: Dinner, Lunch, Main course, Pasta, Supper
declared_fields.Recipe.recipeIngredient: 1 tbsp olive oil; 2 rashers smoked streaky bacon; 1 onion finely chopped; 1 celery stick, finely chopped; 1 medium carrot grated; 2 garlic cloves finely chopped; 500g beef mince; 1 tbsp tomato purée; 2 x 400g cans chopped tomatoes; 1 tbsp clear honey; 500g pack fresh egg lasagne sheets; 400ml crème fraîche
declared_fields.Recipe.recipeInstructions[0].text: Heat the oil in a large saucepan. Use kitchen scissors to snip the bacon into small pieces, or use a sharp knife to chop it on a chopping board. Add the bacon to the pan and cook for just a few mins until starting to turn golden. Add the onion, celery and carrot, and cook over a medium heat for 5 mins, stirring occasionally, until softened.
declared_fields.Recipe.recipeInstructions[1].text: Add the garlic and cook for 1 min, then tip in the mince and cook, stirring and breaking it up with a wooden spoon, for about 6 mins until browned all over.
declared_fields.Recipe.recipeInstructions[2].text: Stir in the tomato purée and cook for 1 min, mixing in well with the beef and vegetables. Tip in the chopped tomatoes. Fill each can half full with water to rinse out any tomatoes left in the can, and add to the pan. Add the honey and season to taste. Simmer for 20 mins.
declared_fields.Recipe.recipeInstructions[3].text: Heat oven to 200C/180C fan/gas 6. To assemble the lasagne, ladle a little of the ragu sauce into the bottom of the roasting tin or casserole dish, spreading the sauce all over the base. Place 2 sheets of lasagne on top of the sauce overlapping to make it fit, then repeat with more sauce and another layer of pasta. Repeat with a further 2 layers of sauce and pasta, finishing with a layer of pasta.
declared_fields.Recipe.recipeInstructions[4].text: Put the crème fraîche in a bowl and mix with 2 tbsp water to loosen it and make a smooth pourable sauce. Pour this over the top of the pasta, then top with the mozzarella. Sprinkle Parmesan over the top and bake for 25–30 mins until golden and bubbling. Serve scattered with basil, if you like.

core: Graydon Hoare created Rust in 2006 while working at Mozilla.
Rust first appeared on January 19, 2012.
adjacent: Hoare started the Rust project due to frustration with broken elevator software in his apartment building.
The language was named after a group of fungi described as 'over-engineered for survival'.
Between 2006 and 2009, Rust was not publicized and was written in Hoare's free time.
Mozilla officially sponsored the Rust project in 2009.
Rust 0.1 became the first public release on January 20, 2012 for Windows, Linux, and MacOS.
Early Rust compiler was written in approximately 38,000 lines of OCaml.
Graydon Hoare stepped down from Rust in 2013.
Rust 1.0, the first stable release, was published on May 15, 2015.
Hoare cited languages from the 1970s, 1980s, and 1990s as influences, including CLU, BETA, Mesa, Erlang, Newsqueak, and others.
Hoare described Rust as 'technology from the past come to save the future from itself.'
The Rust logo was developed in 2011 based on a bicycle chainring.
